title: My submission for March Machine Learning Mania 2025
why_relevant: Directly relevant March Mania writeup using competition-style NCAA data and Brier backtests.
extracted_technique: Build league-specific offensive, defensive, and pace ratings; simulate matchups; use the resulting probabilities as a strong baseline or blend anchor.
query: college basketball prediction efficiency ratings blog brier score matchup model
takeaway: A Bayesian-style efficiency and pace model is a credible prior for this competition and backtests reasonably on historical tournaments. The author explicitly suggests ensembling that baseline with a richer downstream model rather than stopping there.

title: March Madness 2025 Model
why_relevant: Concrete example of a sports-specific rating system that adds prior strength and margin-of-victory handling to Elo.
extracted_technique: Use seeded priors and margin-aware Elo updates instead of naive equal-season starts; convert rating gaps into matchup win probabilities.
query: march madness prediction model efficiency margin of victory blog
takeaway: A margin-aware Elo with informative priors is useful as a feature generator and calibration anchor. It is not enough by itself for top-tier Kaggle accuracy, but it should improve matchup features materially.

title: Categorical Data — xgboost documentation
why_relevant: Confirms GPU-capable XGBoost categorical support and serialization constraints for categorical models.
extracted_technique: Use `tree_method="hist"`, `enable_categorical=True`, `device="cuda"`, preserve dataframe categorical dtypes, and save models in JSON/UBJSON.
takeaway: XGBoost can stay in the shortlist without one-hot explosions, but dtype handling and JSON serialization are non-negotiable. For this competition, XGBoost is best used on dense engineered matchup tables plus fold-safe stat encodings.

title: Categorical features | CatBoost
why_relevant: Official guidance for CatBoost categorical handling and a warning not to one-hot encode upstream.
extracted_technique: Feed raw categorical columns directly, let CatBoost build categorical transforms internally, and use GPU training for speed.
takeaway: CatBoost is the cleanest primary model for this mixed numeric/categorical matchup table. It reduces preprocessing complexity and is well-suited to team, conference, coach, and seed interaction features.

title: Advanced Topics — LightGBM
why_relevant: Official reference for categorical feature support and missing-value behavior in LightGBM.
extracted_technique: Use integer-encoded non-negative categorical columns, rely on native missing handling, and keep LightGBM as a fast diversity model in the ensemble.
takeaway: LightGBM belongs in the shortlist as a complementary learner, not necessarily the headline model. Its categorical path is fast and useful, but category-code hygiene and missing-value conventions must be enforced carefully.

title: brier_score_loss — scikit-learn documentation
why_relevant: Authoritative metric definition for offline evaluation and a reminder that lower is better for probabilistic outputs.
extracted_technique: Optimize and report Brier score on honest season-heldout folds; inspect calibration curves in addition to raw Brier.
query: site:sklearn.org Brier score proper scoring rule documentation
takeaway: The metric is mean squared probability error, so probability calibration matters and clipping/NaN handling must be strict. Because Brier mixes calibration and resolution, model selection should pair it with reliability diagnostics rather than blindly trusting one scalar.
